about: Building blocks for scripts/scenarios.py: how to pick a match type, a venue and a fighter from the menus, which Story points the fixture library should hold, and what is known about launching a cutscene. Pad steps use the harness stage syntax (docs/09-testing-harness.md). 'calibrated' means a run has confirmed the step lands where the name says; an uncalibrated entry is a guess to be checked with --expect-character or the captures. No game data: names and menu steps only.

one-on-one.note: the first match type; the fight and fight-result routes

free-for-all.note: the third match type; the ffa routes

terrordome.note: retail FE ID6; this positional recipe was calibrated with the older unlock state. With every venue unlocked it selects FE ID14 (Hunt's Point); the named harness stress routes and generated Terrordome scenarios inject ChooseVenue(6) before loading. The stress check also asserts its value at StartGame.

the-pit.note: Game.ChooseVenue(19), one step down from the Terrordome on the map; calibrated on macOS 2026-10-14 from the venue-map capture and the fight

fighters.about: The fighter grid is moved with right/down from where the cursor starts. In a one-on-one route player 1 is already READY (the profile's fighter: Blaze, character 4, with the harness's profiles) when the controllersetup(0,0= presses arrive, so the presses after the first A choose the CPU's fighter. Record what a move list picks with `scenarios.py generate ... --expect-character SLOT:N`: the match_start telemetry names the character index each slot got, so a wrong calibration fails instead of fighting the wrong fighter.

calibrated.note: macOS 2026-10-14, at The Pit with --expect-character 0:4 1:14. Presses 2 s apart; a second right 1 s after the first was not taken

story_points.how: no Story save: Main menu -> Story with a new user ID
story_points.cutscenes: the opening movies and the prologue's in-engine scenes, then the character creator

story_points.how: a profile past the prologue; Story -> the crib
crib -> Map -> Shop District -> Stapleton Athletics

cutscenes.files: assets/cinema/*.viv in the dump: sc00 to sc21 and the gf* set (docs/research/widescreen-game-cameras.md, section 4.2)
cutscenes.subsystem: CINEMA::CCinemaSubsystem::LoadScene (its assert strings start near guest 0x29C715); the cinema update sub_00078A40 -> sub_0005BE50 -> the camera sampler sub_00070DF0
cutscenes.loader: sub_00073FD0 (thiscall, the scene's name as its first argument) opens assets/nis_<name>.bin and assets/cinema/<name>.viv; its _enter hook logs every scene as [SCENE] loading <name> and as a recorder 'cinema' event
cutscenes.view_signal: view mode 1 (sub_0001A4E0, a 'view' event with cutscene=true) is set by some shots only: once in sc00, never in sc05 on macOS 2026-10-14. The 'cinema' event is the reliable signal
cutscenes.launch_note: No front-end command names a scene (funccall-catalog: 444 commands). Scenes are played by the game's own developer cinema mode instead, in its developer run module rebuilt from the host (docs/research/dev-module-revival.md).
cutscenes.launcher: RECOMP_SCENE=<name or number>: the developer run module starts at the title screen, plays the scene, and the game returns to the main menu (src/hooks/dev_module.c, scene_launcher.c). `scenarios.py scene <name>` does one, `scenarios.py scenes all` the tour; the overlay's Debug tab has a picker. No save, profile or menu is involved
